refutations.evidence: A is the unused tail of the VDP1 command-list buffer, and its start is exactly the largest list observed, not a fixed limit. Init 0x0600FD94-0x0600FDA0 loads the base from .data 0x06047D1C (=0x060E1000) into the write pointer 0x060CE668. Emitters store a 32-byte command at *0x060CE668 and add #32 with no bound check: 0x060112DC/0x060112F4-0x06011328, and the text routine 0x06011344, which emits one command per character until NUL. The other loaders of 0x060CE668 (0x06016B90, 0x0601F030, 0x0601F788, 0x0602AB86, 0x0602AFC4, 0x0602E9F4) have no compare against a cap. The frame flush at 0x0600FF7C-0x0600FF98 sets r14 = *0x060CE668 - 0x060E1000, copies r14 bytes to 0x25C00000 through 0x0603D22C (it takes the 0x25FE0000/SCU-DMA path, 0x06040D78), and keeps the maximum in .data 0x06047D30. In local/opt001/wramh_27173.bin, 0x06047D30 = 0x00002300. That is 280 commands, with the end command 0x8000 left at 0x060E32E0 (bytes 0x060E32E0 = 80 00 in the dump), so the frame that set it transferred 0x060E1000-0x060E32FF, which includes 0x060E32E4-0x060E32FF (A's first 28 bytes). The read is most likely by DMA, which master-SH-2 read breakpoints would not see. Any frame with one more sprite or glyph writes a full command at 0x060E32E0-0x060E32FF and the end marker at 0x060E3300, inside A. Longer English strings drawn by 0x06011344 add commands. Other dumps' maxima: 0x13E0 (end001), 0x1300 (loc001/loc002); 0x2300 came from the opt001 boot/attract/title/options session. The other end is fine: the pattern allocator (0x0601087A-0x060108E0) is two-ended between 0x060E8000 (*0x06047D20, maps to VRAM 0x8000) and 0x06100000 (*0x06047D24), with cmp/hs checks against the opposite pointer, so pattern staging never goes below 0x060E8000.

The last 12 bytes of C (0x06055824-0x0605582F) are part of a live data structure. The .data pointer array at 0x06057044 = {0x06055824, 0x06056824, 0x06057024, 0x0605702C, 0x06057034}, preceded by header fffe 0002 000a 0007 at 0x0605703C. Mech code stores it into object field +52, e.g. M3CB00A.BIN at base 0x06070800: 0x060734A0 mov.l @(0x060735C4)=0x06057044, then 0x060734AA mov.l r3,@(52,r14). The same literal is in every M2CB/M3CB A/B file except 02 and 07. Entry 0 is a table of 16-byte box records indexed by object byte +102/+103, so record 0 = 0x06055824-0x06055833, and 12 of its bytes are in C. All four CYBER readers of entry 0 skip index 0 (0x060250C2, 0x060251B0, 0x060251E2 and 0x0602664C each tst/bt before mov.l @(52)), and sampled mech code has no unguarded reader, so no read path was found. Still, C's end overlaps a referenced structure. Separately, the damage table at 0x06054424 (4096 bytes, ending exactly at C's start 0x06055424; literal at 0x060257F0) is indexed at 0x060256D4-0x060256EC as (attack byte from entry+13/+14 + (10 or player word +0x190)) * 32 + (rand & 31), with no bound. Index >= 128 would read into C. Observed attack bytes are 0..1 and +0x190 values are 6, 9 and 0x1C (set at 0x0602FC34 from 0x060CFEF8 >> 16, or 31 at 0x0602FC3E), so this needs a level of at least 117 and is not shown reachable.

B's upper boundary 0x060E0EA4 is the low-water mark of the stale stack left by the boot program 0.BIN. 0.BIN's entry is d002 6f03, with literal 0x060E1144 at file offset 0xC (also present at runtime at 0x060A000C), so r15 = 0x060E1144. The block 0x060E0EA4-0x060E1143 holds frame-like data that is byte-identical (md5 1befc3a8...) in every post-load dump and is never rewritten. So B sits just under 0.BIN's deepest observed stack use. A deeper 0.BIN path (for example a boot or read error path) could extend into the top of B, but only before CYBER.BIN runs, and CYBER.BIN contains no reference to the name 0.BIN. This matters only if code is placed in B before or while 0.BIN runs. No CYBER or overlay pointer reaches B: see checked.

checked:
Method: I scanned every disc file for 32-bit big-endian values at 2-byte alignment inside A, B or C, including 0x2xxxxxxx cache-through mirrors (script /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-colinwhite-workspace-personal-cyberbots-saturn-en-translation/0039cb9b-c04e-4750-8bf6-329b9b60dd99/scratchpad/opt003-review/scan.py). I listed PC-relative mov.l literals in 0x060DF8A8-0x060F0000 and 0x260DF8A8-0x260F0000 for CYBER.BIN (base 0x0600D000), every non-graphics BIN at 0x06060000 (OPDEMO, STG0*, KEND, VICTORY and the rest), and M?CB*A at 0x06070800 / M?CB*B at 0x0608B000. I also scanned 19 WRAM-H dumps for runtime values pointing into A, B or C.

CYBER.BIN hits:
- 0x060DF8A8, five times at 0x0604520C/10 and 0x0604700C/10/18: linker section bounds used only by crt0 0x0600D3B0-0x0600D408. The BSS clears are 0x060DF784-0x060DF8A8 and 0x060CC000-0x060DF784. Both data copies have dest == end == 0x060DF8A8, so they copy 0 bytes. No other code references 0x060DF8A8; no heap or sbrk was found.
- 0x060E0000/0x060E1400 at 0x0604CC90: no reference found. It follows the 16-colour palette at 0x0604CC70 (loaded by 0x0600F334 with r5=31) and precedes the byte table at 0x0604CC98.
- 0x060E02CA at 0x0605D886: a word inside 6-byte records, not a pointer.

Overlay and data hits are coincidences inside sprite-part, graphics or audio records: STG0A.BIN 0x1CD70, 0x1CF50 and 0x1D9B8 are 8-byte part records; M?CB 060E0E0E/060E061E/060E06D2 are data; the .LF, .PIX, LOGO.CPK and PL files are graphics or audio. No overlay literal pool holds an A or B address. OPDEMO_0/OPS0_0 0x260E0030 are in non-code data.

BSS variables just below B are bounded:
- 0x060DF878[3] and 0x060DF890[3]: DMA channel arrays indexed 0-2 (0x06040E38-0x06040F24).
- 0x060DF894: 12-byte struct (fields +0/+4/+8).
- 0x060DF8A0: pointer.
- 0x060DF8A4: the live flag.

Near A: 0x060E8000 is the BUP library and work area (0x06036820/24 set 0x060EC000 and 0x060E8000) and a file buffer at 0x06032B12; both run upward. The pattern allocator never goes below 0x060E8000. Below C, the table at 0x06054024 is bounded by (b&0x1F)*32 + (rand&0x1F), so it ends by 0x06054423.

All 19 dumps show A, B and C all zero. Not checked: slave SH-2 code and stack (the game dispatches slave work through 0x06047E7C and 0x21000000 at 0x060105C8), and the pointer behind the frame-0-6000 value 0x060E2608 at 0x06001F3C in wramh_384 (pre-CYBER, outside A).
